subject: Clarification: CCPA/CPRA — telemetry subset & service-provider carveouts
messages:
From: Amira Goldstein <amira@storifyhealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Storify Health Legal <legal@storifyhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 14:05:00 -0400
Subject: Question on CCPA/CPRA classification and telemetry carveouts

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the detailed DPA and list of subprocessors. We are close to finalizing procurement, but our privacy team flagged two items we need explicit confirmation on before legal signs:

1) Service-provider (SP) vs. processor language — for CCPA/CPRA we need explicit commitments that Redwood will act only on instructions and will not retain, use, or sell personal data beyond providing the service (including any telemetry/diagnostic data).

2) Telemetry subset — Storify handles regulated PII; we need to understand exactly what runtime telemetry Redwood collects (prefix lengths, anonymized logs, error traces) and whether any of that could be considered "sale" or "shared" under CCPA. If there are any telemetry examples that might contain identifiers, please indicate retention and access controls.

Could you share an annotated redline (or a short carveout) so our counsel can review? Also please attach the current subprocessor list and any SOC2 artifacts mapping telemetry categories to retention.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we are hoping to reach SO to sign this week.

Best,
Amira
Legal Ops — Storify Health

[Attachment: request-checklist.pdf]

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Amira Goldstein <amira@storifyhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on CCPA/CPRA classification and telemetry carveouts

Hi Amira — thanks for the note and the checklist. Looping in Kimberly (privacy counsel) and Marissa (contracts) to provide concrete language and the subprocessor artifacts. Quick answers up front:

- Redwood commits to the standard service-provider obligations in our DPA: we process per documented customer instructions and do not \"sell\" customer personal information. Our telemetry is categorized and treated as operational metadata; we do not tie telemetry to marketing or advertising uses.

- That said, to avoid ambiguity for state-level privacy teams we can propose a short addendum that: (a) enumerates telemetry categories (runtime metrics, error traces, aggregated usage); (b) states retention windows and de-identification controls for each; and (c) confirms that telemetry will not be used in any manner constituting a \"sale\" under CCPA/CPRA.

Kimberly/Marissa — can you confirm if we can ship the subprocessor list (v2027-07) and the SOC2 mapping doc and provide a 2-paragraph redline that Amira can attach? Timeline: if we can get the language out today, Storify legal wants to review tomorrow.

Thanks,
Priyom
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

[Attachment: request-checklist.pdf (forwarded)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Amira Goldstein <amira@storifyhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on CCPA/CPRA classification and telemetry carveouts

Priyom / Marissa / Amira — I reviewed the ask and prepared a short proposed addendum and an annotated diff of the DPA. Key points in the proposed language (attached as proposed-sp-language-diff.docx):

- Definition: \"Telemetry\" is defined narrowly to include (i) runtime aggregate metrics (request counts, p95 latency), (ii) anonymized error traces where any PII is removed or hashed, (iii) prefix-level KV cache metadata (sequence lengths and hit rates) that does not include utterance text beyond a fixed 64-byte prefix used for debugging.

- Non-sale certification: \"Provider represents and warrants that telemetry, as defined herein, will not be sold, shared, or otherwise monetized in a manner constituting a 'sale' under CCPA/CPRA; telemetry will be used solely for service operation, security, and performance improvement.\"

- Retention & access: Default telemetry retention is 30 days for detailed traces, 90 days for aggregated metrics; access is restricted to SRE and privacy-authorized engineers. We can provide onshore log export for Storify on request (onboarding + charge).

- Subprocessor evidence: attached redwood_subprocessor_list_v2027-07.pdf; SOC2 mapping links are included in the Drive link we will share.

Where I expect negotiation: Storify may request a shorter retention for traces or a categorical carveout for certain regulated fields. If Storify requires onshore-only telemetry processing, we can offer an onshore-fallback for telemetry ingestion on Dedicated or Private deployments as a commercial add-on (see note in the proposed addendum).

Marissa — please attach the subprocessor list and the annotated diff to send to Amira. I also created a short "talking points" doc so sales can explain the difference between telemetry metadata and customer content during the counterparty review.

-Kim
Senior Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-sp-language-diff.docx (contains redlines), redwood_subprocessor_list_v2027-07.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Amira Goldstein <amira@storifyhealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Re: Question on CCPA/CPRA classification and telemetry carveouts

Amira — attaching the proposed addendum and current subprocessor list.

Quick summary for Storify legal:
- We've inserted a narrow telemetry definition and a non-sale warranty.
- Default retention windows: detailed traces 30 days / aggregated metrics 90 days. We can shorten or provide onshore-only processing for telemetry at additional cost.
- Redwood will provide SOC2 mapping and can initiate an onshore log-export pilot if you need immediate evidence.

Next steps: please confirm whether (1) the telemetry definition as drafted is acceptable, and (2) you need an onshore-processing clause (we will share pricing and timeline). If both OK, Marissa will incorporate into the DPA and circulate a final redline for signature.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference
